vocabulary.term: What are you going to do?
vocabulary.example: What are you going to do this weekend?

grammar.explanation_en: Use 'going to' for plans you already decided before speaking: 'I'm going to visit Busan next week.' Use 'will' for decisions made at the moment of speaking, promises, or predictions: 'I will help you' (spontaneous), 'I think it will rain' (prediction).
grammar.explanation_ko: 'going to'는 말하기 전에 이미 정해둔 계획에 씁니다: 'I'm going to visit Busan next week.'(다음 주에 부산 갈 예정이에요). 'will'은 말하는 순간 결정한 일, 약속, 예측에 씁니다: 'I will help you'(즉흥적 결정), 'I think it will rain'(예측).

examples.en: I'm going to study abroad next year.

examples.ko: 저는 이 팀이 이길 것 같아요.

reading.title: Plans for Next Month
reading.text: Next month, I am going to move to a new apartment. I already found a nice place near my office. I plan to buy new furniture too. My friend promised she will help me on moving day. I think it will be a busy but exciting month.
reading.text_ko: 다음 달에 저는 새 아파트로 이사할 예정이에요. 이미 회사 근처에 좋은 집을 찾았어요. 새 가구도 살 계획이에요. 친구가 이사하는 날 도와주기로 약속했어요. 바쁘지만 신나는 한 달이 될 것 같아요.

explanation.en: The text says 'I am going to move to a new apartment.'
explanation.ko: 본문에 'move to a new apartment'라고 나옵니다.

explanation.en: The text says 'My friend promised she will help me on moving day.'
explanation.ko: 본문에 'help me on moving day'라고 나옵니다.

explanation.en: The text says 'a nice place near my office.'
